1. A theology of the imago dei
2. Is image substance, function, or relationship?
3. Image as Identity
4. Revelatory or Canonical Interpretation of the Imago Dei
5. The Canonical Imago Dei
6. The Identity Interpretation and the Christian Tradition

"The imago dei is humanity's identity", namely an identity that is "basic to all human existence" [1]. According to this interpretation of the creation account, humanity was created to serve as an earthly image of God, "God in the world". As such, attributes of God, are synonymous with human attributes. Why don't we exhibit these attributes then, but instead exhibit other more reprehensible attributes?
